scope: Independent reconsideration of all eight existing technical conclusions; prior consultations known but no fresh response available. Decisions remain reviewable after new results.

integer_codec.basis: Original numeric tokens preserve precision. JSON Schema mathematical integrality creates a concrete interoperability requirement. Bounded native-token adaptation can satisfy both without source coercion.

generation_shapes.basis: All traced required generation flows fit ordinary nonrecursive records/arrays. References and variants require more provider schema emission and testing; existing shared codec validation remains reusable.

aggregate_type.basis: An internal aggregate with no observed or exported payload needs no source type. Source-visible values still require unique expected nominal F, avoiding unrelated declaration-dependent lookup.

resource_deadline.basis: The fixed no-loser-cancellation/live-lease constraints do not imply eventual exit. Separating host kill from language cleanup expresses the operational limit without adding runtime termination policy.

sequential_map.basis: The supplied native algorithm and observed order/failure behavior match the required sequential semantics. Indices and private completion boxes protect legal callable then fields.

fixture_queue.basis: Repeated equal-argument calls need ordered supplied outcomes. Shared FIFO supports those scripts in existing syntax. It requires one explicit canonical test scheduler and separate native interleaving conformance.

generic_checking.basis: No type-bound syntax is approved. Checking every branch of reachable concrete instances preserves useful generic operations while making use-site errors and termination restrictions explicit.

promise_payloads.basis: Native thenable assimilation is an observed semantic hazard for legal records. Universal private promise-boundary protection avoids source-name restrictions and does not dictate the physical layout of ordinary fields.
